campaigns.title: Delhi MACT Ecosystem Audit
campaigns.description: One coordinated RTI sweep (Oct 2025 - Feb 2026) across every institution in Delhi's crash-compensation chain: Transport Dept, DSLSA/DLSAs, Delhi Police districts, MACT courts in all district court complexes, and MoRTH. Probes hit-and-run scheme uptake, legal aid, claim pendency, and DAR/FDAR compliance with Supreme Court directions (Rajesh Tyagi v. Jaibir Singh; Gohar Mohammed).

threads.questions_summary: Legal aid applications/approvals/rejections for MACT cases; lawyer-assignment time; MACT panel size; DVCS 2018 applications and amounts; hit-and-run scheme applications and beneficiary counts; SOPs; awareness campaigns.

events.detail: Forwarded online to all DLSAs for district-level queries

responses.summary: Answered 5 of 21 queries centrally, rest forwarded to DLSAs. Confirmed NO panel of lawyers specifically for MACT cases exists (2022-2024) and NO SOP for legal aid in motor accident cases. Gave disbursement totals - but supplied IDENTICAL figures for DVCS road-victim disbursals (Q10) and Hit-and-Run Scheme disbursals (Q14), while also stating it only disburses under DVCS 2018: internally inconsistent.

findings: No MACT-specific lawyer panel exists anywhere in DSLSA (2022-2024); candidates for 'MACT panel' merely need 5 years of civil practice.
No SOP exists for legal aid in motor accident cases.
DSLSA's reply gives identical rupee figures for two different schemes (DVCS Q10 and Hit-and-Run Q14) - an internal inconsistency worth a follow-up RTI or appeal.

threads.subject: DAR/IAR/FAR filing compliance in road-crash cases, FY 2022-23 to 2024-25
threads.questions_summary: District-wise fatal and non-fatal crash counts; DARs filed within/beyond 90 days; IARs within/beyond 50 days; FARs within 24 hours; completeness of DAR documentation; MACT rectification directions. These deadlines are the Gohar Mohammed (SC, 2023) / MV (Amendment) Act framework.

events.detail: Filed online; distributed to district PIOs
West, Shahdara, Kashmere Gate Metro replies

responses.summary: 'Very lengthy, time consuming, requires diversion of manpower' - offered record inspection at police stations, figures only.
Same deflection; inspection at DCP office within a month.
Same deflection; visit police stations 10am-5pm.
Same deflection; also pointed to Delhi Police website.
Deflection - and admitted the MACT Inspector's records are 'not available in the requisite format'.
Gave district crash counts (see key_figures) but said DAR/IAR timeliness records are 'not maintained separately' and ruled remaining queries outside 'information' u/s 2(f).
Tiny jurisdiction; 1 fatal crash (FY 2022-23, DAR within 90 days, FAR within 24h), 1 non-fatal (IAR within 50 days). The only police unit that answered the compliance questions as asked.

key_figures.metric: Fatal accidents, West District
Simple (non-fatal) accidents, West District
Police district responses that deflected to inspection
key_figures.value: 5 of 7 district replies on record (+ HQ silence)

findings: No Delhi Police district could (or would) state how many DARs were filed within the 90-day legal deadline - the single most consequential compliance number for crash victims.
Five of seven district replies used the identical 'voluminous - come inspect' template, suggesting a coordinated non-answer.
West District's own numbers show fatal crashes declining 182 -> 142 (2022-2025).

verification.notes: Confirm whether other districts (Central, New Delhi, Rohini, Outer etc.) replied at all - folder has 7 districts + Metro.

threads.subject: MACT pendency, disposal statistics, disposal time, and FDAR/CTAP/MCTAP compliance (Rajesh Tyagi directions), FY 2020-21 to 2024-25
threads.questions_summary: Pending cases by year/type; cases pending >3 years with reasons; disposals by method; average disposal time; compliance with SC targets (120-day FDAR disposal, 6-12 month standard disposal); DAR filing within 30 days under the scheme; insurance settlement within 30 days of DAR.

events.detail: Filed with PDSJ Central (Tis Hazari); parallel paper application to Delhi HC Registrar General
RTI Central THC transferred online to all district court PIOs

responses.summary: Fullest reply in the corpus: pendency 1,126 (460 fatal/663 injury/3 DoP); DAR filed within 30 days vs beyond - 32 vs 1,543 over 2020-25; insurance settled within 30 days of DAR: 48 vs 392 contested; disposal-time claim 'within 12 months' for all categories (inconsistent with its own >5yr table: 114 of 2,111 disposals took >5 years).
Pendency 427 (>3yr: 42); FDAR disposals: Nil; 6-12-month disposals 1,168/3,661; >2yr disposals 1,731/3,661 (47%); >5yr 687/3,661 (19%); DAR delay 'average 2-3 months'.

Pendency table by year/type; 321 cases >3 years (159 fatal); disposals FY20-25: 1,034 contested / 1,604 settled / 58 dismissed; FDAR disposals: Nil; 6-12-month disposals 1,099/4,600; >2yr 1,251/4,600; delay reasons, disposal-time and DAR-timeliness data 'not maintained'.

Pendency 1,840 (per NJDG), 586 pending >3 years, 258 pending witness examination; ~1,835 disposals contested/compromised/settled; everything else - FDAR/CTAP compliance, disposal times, DAR timeliness, insurance conduct - 'no such data maintained'.
Handwritten reply. Pendency ~1,409 (NJDG); ~519 pending >3 years; ~1,458 disposed; FDAR, disposal-time, DAR and insurance queries all 'no such data maintained'. Digits uncertain - verify.

MACT-02: 661 pending, 118 >3yr, 842 disposed since 2020; qualitative delay reasons given (HC stays, witness/counsel availability). Second court (per NJDG): ~2,076 pending, ~170 >3yr, ~2,141 disposed. Disposal-time and FDAR data 'not maintained'.

Pendency 340 (38 death/298 injury/4 DoP), 432 >3yr (figure inconsistent with pendency - verify); delay-reason and disposal-time queries refused as 'creation of information'; ONE case disposed under FDAR ever; 435 contested / 156 mediation / 1,411 Lok Adalat disposals.

Court only created 26.08.2025; gave pendency snapshot (1,649 incl. DAR/execution/misc categories, 567 fatal/533 injury) and declined historic queries as pre-dating its existence. Delay-reason data: maintaining it 'not envisaged under RTI' (s.2(f)/s.2(j) argument).
Pendency 1,578 (559 fatal/810 injury), 431 >3yr; ONE case disposed under FDAR; delay reasons refused (Rule 7(vii)); disposal stats 'in public domain'; judicial-proceedings exemption (9(x)) invoked.
Pendency 1,259 (403 fatal/671 injury), 485 >3yr; ZERO FDAR cases; same exemption pattern as MACT-01.

Disposals taking >5 years, Central MACT-02

findings: FDAR/CTAP/MCTAP - the Supreme Court's fast-track machinery from Rajesh Tyagi - has produced TWO disposals across every Delhi MACT court that answered, in five years. The scheme is functionally dead in the very jurisdiction where it was designed.
Only 2% of DARs reached Central district MACT-01 within the 30-day scheme deadline (32 vs 1,543).

No MACT court maintains the compliance statistics the SC's Gohar Mohammed/Rajesh Tyagi framework presupposes: disposal-time registers, DAR-timeliness logs, FDAR compliance data - 'no such data maintained', across the board.

Two court complexes (Patiala House, Dwarka) invoked Delhi District Court RTI Rules 7(vi)/(vii)/9(x) to refuse delay-reason data as 'creation of information' - an appealable position given the SC's own direction that this data be tracked.
~3,100+ MACT cases pending over 3 years across reporting courts alone (several districts missing).
